title: Caro-Kann Defence
description: A solid Black repertoire against 1.e4. The bishop gets out before ...e6, you hit the centre with ...c5 or ...d5, and your position stays free of weaknesses.
source: Main lines as recommended by GothamChess and standard Caro-Kann theory. Every one of your moves checked with Stockfish 17.1.

lines.name: Advance Variation: the Short System
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 Be3 Nd7 O-O Ne7 c4 dxc4 Na3 Nd5
lines.idea: In the Advance: bishop out to f5 first, then ...e6, then hit the base of White's chain with ...c5. Knights go to d7 and e7 (f6 is taken), and if White opens the centre, plant a knight on d5.

lines.name: Advance Variation: White castles and plays c3
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 O-O Nc6 c3 cxd4 cxd4 Nge7 Nc3 Nc8
lines.idea: Against the quiet c3 set-up: ...c5 and ...Nc6 to hit d4, trade on d4 to open the c-file, then knight from e7 to c8 to b6 to shore up d5.

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4 Qb3 Qd7 Nd2 e6 Ngf3 Bxf3 Nxf3 Bd6
lines.idea: In the Exchange, keep a pawn on d5. The bishop goes to g4 because f5 is covered. Meet Qb3 with ...Qd7, trade White's f3 knight and f4 bishop, then attack on the queenside with ...b5-b4.

lines.name: Panov Attack: White plays c4
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Be7 cxd5 Nxd5 Bd3 Nc6 O-O O-O Re1 Bf6
lines.idea: Against the Panov, let White have an isolated d-pawn. Put a knight on d5 in front of it, pile up on it with ...Nc6 and ...Bf6, and trade pieces: the fewer pieces left, the weaker that pawn gets.

lines.name: Classical: 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bd2 Ngf6 O-O-O Be7
lines.idea: In the Classical: take on e4, bishop to f5 with tempo, back to g6 and h7 when kicked. Answer h4 with ...h6, put knights on d7 and f6, trade light-squared bishops, then ...e6, ...Be7 and castle.

lines.name: Two Knights: 2.Nc3 and 3.Nf3
lines.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6 d4 Nf6 Bd3 dxe4 Nxe4 Qxd4 c3 Qd8
lines.idea: Against the Two Knights: pin with ...Bg4 and trade it for the f3 knight, then ...e6 and ...Nf6. If d4 is left without a defender, open the d-file and take it.

lines.name: Fantasy Variation: 3.f3
lines.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4 Ne7 Qd3 b6 Ne2 Ba6 Qe3 O-O
lines.idea: Against the Fantasy, ...e6 and ...Bb4 pins the knight that guards e4. The king's knight goes to e7, and ...b6 with ...Ba6 trades off your bad bishop.

explain.e4|c6: The Caro-Kann. The c6 pawn prepares ...d5, so you can challenge e4 with a pawn that is backed up. Unlike the French with ...e6, it leaves your c8 bishop's diagonal open.
explain.e4 c6 d4|d5: Challenge e4 straight away. Because c6 backs up d5, if White takes on d5 you recapture with a pawn and keep a pawn in the centre.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5|Bf5: Get the light-squared bishop outside your pawn chain BEFORE playing ...e6. This is the whole point of the Caro-Kann. From f5 it watches e4, d3, c2 and b1.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3|e6: Now ...e6 is safe, because the bishop is already out. The pawn backs up d5 and opens your dark-squared bishop.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2|c5: Your key break in the Advance. White's pawn chain d4-e5 rests on d4, so hit d4 with ...c5 and the chain starts to wobble.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 Be3|Nd7: Develop the queen's knight to d7. From there it backs up ...c5 and eyes the e5 pawn. Your other knight will go via e7.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 Be3 Nd7: The king's knight goes to e7, because the e5 pawn covers f6. From e7 it can jump to c6 or d5 later.
Take the pawn. That hands your pieces the d5 square, a perfect outpost right in front of White's pawns.
Plant the knight on d5. No White pawn can kick it from there, and it hits e3 and b4. Next ...Be7 and castle.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 O-O|Nc6: Develop with pressure: the knight joins the c5 pawn in hitting d4.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 O-O Nc6: Now trade on d4. This opens the c-file, a highway for a rook on c8 later.
The king's knight goes to e7, since f6 is covered by the e5 pawn. It is heading for c8 and then b6.
Reroute the knight. From c8 it goes to b6, guarding d5 a second time and eyeing c4, and it clears e7 for your bishop.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5|cxd5: Recapture with the c-pawn and keep a pawn in the centre. This is why ...c6 came first.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3|Nf6: Develop the king's knight. It guards d5 and h7.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4: With f5 covered by the d3 bishop, your bishop comes out to g4 instead, where it attacks White's queen on d1.
Guard b7 with your queen along the seventh rank. She stays close to your king as well.
Open your dark-squared bishop and make d5 rock-solid.
Trade the bishop for that knight. It was White's best guard of e5, the square he would love to use.
Challenge White's best piece, the f4 bishop. Next, castle and push ...b5 and ...b4 to attack White's c3 pawn: the minority attack.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4|Nf6: Defend d5 with a piece and develop at the same time.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3|e6: Back up d5 and open your dark-squared bishop. Here your c8 bishop stays home for a while, and that's fine.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3|: Develop and get ready to castle. Later the bishop can come to f6 and hit d4.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3: Take back with the knight. White now has an isolated pawn on d4: no pawn next to it can ever defend it. Your knight sits right in front of it, and no pawn can kick it.
Develop and add pressure on d4, the isolated pawn.
Castle. Your king is safe, and both knights work against d4.
The bishop comes to f6: a third piece hitting d4. It also guards your king's side.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3|dxe4: Take on e4. White can't hold it, and the trade gives your c8 bishop an open road.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4|Bf5: Develop with a threat: the bishop attacks the e4 knight.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3|Bg6: Retreat to g6 and stay on the same diagonal towards c2 and b1. If White ever takes on g6, you recapture hxg6 and your rook gets the h-file.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4: Give the bishop an escape square on h7 before h5 arrives.
Develop the queen's knight to d7. It covers e5, so White's knight can't land there, and it leaves f6 free for your other knight.
The bishop drops back to h7, still on its diagonal towards d3 and c2.
Trade. White has to bring his queen forward to take back.
With your bishop gone, ...e6 costs nothing. It opens your dark-squared bishop and guards d5 and f5.
Develop the king's knight. It guards d5 and h7.
Develop and get ready to castle short. You have no weaknesses at all, which is the Caro-Kann's promise.
explain.e4 c6 Nc3|d5: Same idea as always: hit e4 with a pawn that's backed up.
explain.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3|Bg4: Pin the f3 knight to the queen. You are happy to trade this bishop for that knight, which guards d4 and e5.
explain.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3|Bxf3: Take the knight. Retreating to h5 would invite g4 and a pawn storm against your bishop.
explain.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3|e6: Back up d5 and open your dark-squared bishop.
explain.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6 d4|: Develop and add another guard to d5.
explain.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6 d4: Swap off White's e-pawn. That opens the d-file towards d4.
Take the d4 pawn. You are a pawn up.
Bring the queen home. You are a pawn up. White has some extra development in return, so castle quickly with ...Be7 and ...O-O.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3|e6: Stay calm and solid. ...e6 backs up d5 and opens your dark-squared bishop, which is about to pin.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3|Bb4: Pin the knight to the king. A pinned knight can't really defend e4.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4|Ne7: Knight to e7, not f6, where it would run into e5. From e7 it backs up d5 and can jump to g6 to hit the f4 bishop.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4 Ne7 Qd3|b6: Prepare ...Ba6, to trade off your light-squared bishop, the one stuck behind e6.
explain.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4 Ne7 Qd3 b6: The bishop hits White's queen on d3, and behind her the e2 knight and the f1 bishop.
Castle. Your pieces are out and your king is safe, while White's king is still in the centre.

replies.|e4: White opens with the king's pawn.
replies.e4 c6|d4: White takes the whole centre with two pawns.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5|e5: The Advance. White pushes past your d5 pawn, grabbing space and taking the f6 square away from your knight.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5|Nf3: White develops calmly, guarding d4 and e5.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6|Be2: White develops quietly and gets ready to castle.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5|Be3: The Short System: White guards d4 with his bishop and keeps everything solid.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 Be3 Nd7: White opens the position before you have castled, hitting your d5 pawn.
White plans to win the pawn back with Nxc4.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5|O-O: White castles and leaves his bishop on c1 for now.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5 O-O Nc6: White props up d4 with another pawn.
White recaptures and keeps a pawn on d4.
White develops and puts more pressure on d5.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5|exd5: The Exchange Variation. White swaps off the centre pawns.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5|Bd3: White's bishop aims at h7, and it also stops your bishop from coming to f5.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6|c3: White guards d4 with a pawn.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6|Bf4: White's bishop takes the b8-h2 diagonal.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4: White's queen side-steps and attacks b7, which your c8 bishop used to guard.
White recaptures with the other knight.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5|c4: The Panov Attack. White hits d5 again and aims for fast development, even at the cost of an isolated pawn.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3: White aims at h7, getting ready to attack.
White's rook takes the e-file and eyes e6.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5|Nc3: White defends e4 with a knight instead of pushing or trading.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4|Nxe4: White recaptures with the knight, which now sits in the centre.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5|Ng3: The knight steps back and attacks your bishop.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6|h4: White threatens h5, which would trap your bishop.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4: White pushes on and kicks the bishop.
White gets ready to castle queenside.
White castles long. With the kings on opposite sides, both sides will attack.
replies.e4 c6|Nc3: White develops first and keeps d2-d4 in reserve.
replies.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4|h3: White asks your bishop what it wants to do.
replies.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3|Qxf3: White recaptures with the queen, which now eyes f7 down the open f-file.
replies.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4 h3 Bxf3 Qxf3 e6 d4: White develops, but now nothing defends d4.
White kicks your queen and gains time for development.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5|f3: The Fantasy. White guards e4 with a pawn and wants a big centre.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4|Bf4: White develops his bishop to an active square.
replies.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4 Ne7|Qd3: White guards e4 again and gets ready to castle long.
